correctness.rationale: The only pairs at distance three are x_i,y_j for i≠j. Their three geodesics have edge sets {a_i,h,b_j}, {a_i,a_j,c_j}, {c_i,b_i,b_j}; every other shortest path has at most two edges. Thus whenever at least two a-edges (respectively b-edges) are selected, the chosen c-indices must avoid their indices; with the spine present the two end-index sets must have one empty or be the same singleton. These necessary and sufficient conditions give the disjoint binomial counts. Independently, with c-indices avoiding A∪B, the per-page weight is W=1+3z+z²; inclusion–exclusion for |A|,|B|≤1 gives V=W^r−2[(1+2z)^r+rz(1+z)(1+2z)^(r−1)]+(1+z)^r+(2rz+rz²)(1+z)^(r−1)+r(r−1)z²(1+z)^(r−2). This verifies the stated total after substituting z=1. With no spine and both end-index sets large, |S|≤r+|A∩B|≤2r, with 2r forcing all a- and b-edges. The other no-spine cases reach at most r+2. With the spine the size r+3 is attained only by both ends of one page and all c-edges. This gives the small cases and the tie at r=3. An independent shortest-path and subset computation for r=2,3,4,5 found 6,18,36,60 obstructions; totals 73,297,1195,4949; and top coefficients 2,4,1,1.
residual_risks: The checks for small r corroborate the obstruction argument, not the all-r claim on their own.

checked_sources: The inspected grid/partial-cube comparisons and independently enumerated small extremizers
value.rationale: The diameter-three book is a natural family with many competing geodesics between page interiors. The polynomial counts every size of admissible set, beyond a scalar maximum, and the case analysis explains a switch from spine-based optima to a unique spine-free optimum, with a tie at exactly three pages. Thus it supplies a usable exact enumerator and structural information, not a finite list or a routine restatement of the grid maximum.
residual_risks: Value is for this family and predicate; no extension to arbitrary prisms or polygonal books is shown.
